newsitem.title: UK: Euro fuel oil boosted by US swap buys, Asia strength.
newsitem.headline: Euro fuel oil boosted by US swap buys, Asia strength.

text.p: European fuel oil markets were boosted on Friday by higher swaps, which had risen on the back of soaring crude and the strength of Asian and U.S. markets, traders said.
Dutch dealers returned from their Ascension Day break to find Rotterdam barges $4 stronger, trading at $86 and $86.50 on short covering, after swaps rose in response to Singapore papers strength.
Some 20,000 tonnes traded in the morning before activity tailed off and prices slipped back to $85/$86.
The picture was distorted by the thinness of the market, since many majors were not at their desks and traders were gathered at an industry convention in the south of France.
Activity was more marked in the Mediterranean, where bunker deals were done and traders were believed trying to put together high sulphur cracked cargoes to take to the Far East.

A northern French cargo of 25,000 tonnes of high density material was believed sold on Thursday to a trader, who also bought 45,000 tonnes of bunker spec from Cartagena at a price heard to be $80.50 fob.
A cargo from Coruna was heard sold to cover a short into a Portuguese utility for $77 fob.
Higher U.S. one percent prices had led American buyers to push up European cargo swaps. It was unclear how far behind physical prices trailed since supplies are tight in the prompt period.
A 45,000 tonne cargo of one percent was sold on Thursday from Britain to a trader on a floating price basis, loading 29-31 May and bound for Italy.
